To find the order $\beta$ such that Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information $I_\alpha(X; Y)$ converges to the Rényi entropy $H_\beta(X)$ as $\mathsf{snr} \to \infty$, we recall the expression for Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information:
$$I_\alpha(X; Y) = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 1} \log \int \left( \sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} dy$$

For the additive Gaussian noise channel $Y = \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} X + Z$, the conditional density is:
$$p(y|x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$
so that:
$$p(y|x)^\alpha = (2\pi)^{-\alpha/2} \exp\left( -\frac{\alpha(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$

In the high-SNR regime ($\mathsf{snr} \to \infty$), the separation between adjacent support points scaled by $\sqrt{\mathsf{snr}}$ tends to infinity, meaning the Gaussian bumps in the mixture $\sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha$ become non-overlapping. Consequently:
$$\left( \sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} \approx \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha} \left( p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} = \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$

Integrating over $y$ yields:
$$\int \left( \sum_x P(x) p(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} dy \xrightarrow{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha}$$

Substituting this back into the expression for $I_\alpha(X; Y)$:
$$\lim_{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} I_\alpha(X; Y) = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 1} \log \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha} = \frac{1}{1 - 1/\alpha} \log \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha}$$

Comparing this with the definition of the Rényi entropy of order $\beta$:
$$H_\beta(X) = \frac{1}{1 - \beta} \log \sum_x P(x)^\beta$$
we identify:
$$\beta = \frac{1}{\alpha}$$

ANSWER: 1/\alpha
